handoff: Review#1 F1–F5 fixed. Blocking: F1 AC4 'continues' fails, because B's first tick re-intakes a branchless checked-out story (intake_story, new local branch; reproduced). F2: the record is placed before the branch fetch/branch_diverged and the take receipt, so a retry keeps the local copy and loses the rewritten restart (T5a). Minor: crash-window guard, double attempt bump, fetch before claim CAS; nits.

findings.title: A branchless story checked out on B is intaken again on B's next tick; AC4's 'and continues' is untested and false
findings.detail:
AC4: 'Given a story with no branch handed over by A, when checkout runs on B, then it unpacks the record without the ancestry check and continues.' The test stops after checkout. I copied the AC4 test into a scratch file and added one B.tick(). The decisions were [{unit:'gh-12', rule:'remote.intake', kind:'intake_story', ok:true}], `git branch` on B listed a new local `gh-12-branchless`, and the take receipt was not applied (state still A's running review#2 run). Cause: the snapshot finds stories only from worktrees, the base and the main checkout, so decide/index.ts intake() treats gh-12 as unknown. The act's skip (act/lifecycle.ts:229) fires only when the branch exists on the remote, so it creates a worktree and a fresh spec.md with status new. The test also covers only 'branch deleted, trailer present', never a record without Norn-Branch-Commit.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Make a story held here, with run state in the machine dir, known to the snapshot or intake (or skip intake for a story with a claim or record ref). Extend AC4 with a tick that asserts no intake_story and that review#2 resumes. Add a case whose record has no Norn-Branch-Commit.

findings.title: The rewritten verdict is lost when checkout fails after placing the record and before writing the take receipt
findings.detail:
The order is: place() and setRecordRef (:277-278), then the branch fetch, which can throw 'fetch failed' (:288), then worktree checkout, which can throw branch_diverged (:316). Only after that do rewrittenSince and takeReceipt run (:320-321). branch_diverged is a likely path for B24: a force-pushed branch meeting an older local branch here. On the retry the claim is mine and the run-state dir exists, so keepLocal gives unpacked:false and rewrittenSince returns null (:162). There is no `rewritten` and no restart, and the step resumes on code that is gone (T5a: 'When it is not … restarts the current step as a new attempt, saying why'). A crash in the same window ends the same way. T5 also wants the take receipt 'before any other effect'.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Decide the rewrite before placing (head is known after the branch fetch, so fetch the branch first or compute ancestry from the fetched objects), and write the take receipt, with `rewritten`, into the staged or just-placed record before anything that can fail. Or persist a pending-take marker until it is written. Add a test: force-pushed branch plus a diverged local branch on B, then fix and re-checkout, which must still restart.

findings.title: No decide guard for a held story whose record is not yet placed
findings.detail:
If the process dies between acquireClaim and place() (claim held, record not placed), and a story worktree already exists here with no run-state dir, decideUnit/startStoryUnit emits start_unit with initialState: a start-over (S2). If an old run-state dir from an earlier stint exists instead, the tick resumes that stale cursor, and the stale-push do_instead (keepLocal) would push it on top of the newer record. The window is narrow, since place() follows the claim synchronously, and on a first checkout there is no worktree yet (start.no_worktree), so this is minor. record-ref.ts place() is also not atomic over an existing dest (rename dest→old, then staging→dest; moved from unpackRecordSync), and a throw from place/setRecordRef after the claim surfaces as a raw error without saying the claim is held.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Hold start_unit for a claimed story that has a record ref but no state (or that has a pending-take marker). Wrap place/setRecordRef failures in a failure() that says the claim is held and what to run.

findings.title: Double attempt bump when unapplied receipts move the cursor before the take
findings.detail:
With an unapplied `rework` in the record, applying it enters implement#3. The rewritten take then re-enters implement as #4 ('restarting implement as attempt 4', test :263). implement#3 never ran and judged no code, so attempts and visits drift by one. Rules that count visits (e.g. GR8 refineFinished, visits >= 2) can then misread a just-restarted step. checkout's restartOf also runs plain applyReceipts across a `round` receipt, which the tick applies separately, so the prediction can differ from the tick. Output, state and brief agree with each other.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Restart only when the cursor the take meets is the one the record was written at, or one that already ran a session. Otherwise mark the newly entered attempt as the rewritten restart without a second enterStep.

findings.title: The record is fetched before the claim CAS: an expired but live holder can push in between
findings.detail:
Moving the fetch before the claim (the right call for F1) means a holder whose claim expired but which is still running can push a newer record between the fetch and acquireClaim. The checkout then places the older record. Its push is later refused as stale, and following the Check item's do_instead (`norn story checkout`, keepLocal) pushes the older state on top of the newer record (parent kept, content overwritten).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: After the claim lands, re-read the remote ref (ls-remote). If it moved, re-stage, or refuse and release.

findings.title: F2 slot: details and comment drift
findings.detail:
Five points: (a) recordPushItem's comment says observe reports the refusal only while the claim is here, but observe and the view report it until a tick drops the slot. (b) A later non-stale failure keeps the old item with an out-of-date lease. (c) act/index.ts:159 writes placeholder step '?' and attempt 1, because `this.written.get('record:…')` never matches. (d) RECORD_PUSH_EFFECT and recordPushSlot now sit between actFailureItem's doc comment and the function. (e) restartOf runs applyReceipts twice over nearly the same list; the `r.rewritten &&` check in apply.ts:186 is redundant; checkout resolves `head` even without a record (extra spawn in recovery-claim-lost.txt); a killed process leaves `.<story>.unpack-<pid>` behind.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Tidy as convenient.

findings.title: Checkout's printed status still shows the pre-restart attempt beside the 'attempt 3' line
findings.detail:
units[].handoff renders state.json before the take is applied, so it shows review attempt 2 next to `restarted: …attempt 3`. Also, the story unit is the only unit restarted. In a sliced story the story cursor sits at `slices`, so the restart changes nothing while the slice cursors judged code on the gone commit. A stuck or $done unit prints no notice of the rewrite. This matches D10's literal 'restart the cursor's step'; worth recording as a known limit.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Render the status after the predicted restart, or add '(applied by the next tick)'; note the sliced-story limit in the spec or handoff.
